extra.message: Server-Side Template Injection (SSTI) leading to remote code execution. The user-controlled 'name' query parameter is interpolated into the 'content' string (line 38) and then passed to jinja2.Template(content).render(). Because Template() compiles the string as a Jinja2 template, an attacker can inject template syntax such as ?name={{7*7}} (evaluated to 49) or sandbox-escape payloads like {{ ''.__class__.__mro__[1].__subclasses__() }} to execute arbitrary Python code on the server. The user input must never be used to construct a template; it should be passed as a rendered variable with autoescaping enabled.

cwe: CWE-94: Improper Control of Generation of Code (Code Injection)

extra.message:
Reflected Cross-Site Scripting (XSS). The user-supplied 'name' query parameter is concatenated directly into an HTML string via an f-string (f"

Hello, {name}!...

") without any HTML escaping, and the route returns the result as an HTMLResponse (response_class=HTMLResponse, line 18). An attacker can supply ?name= to execute arbitrary JavaScript in victims' browsers. The value of the external 'public_ip' service (also interpolated unescaped on the same line) is likewise reflected, compounding the risk if that service is compromised. Use an autoescaping template engine or html.escape() on all interpolated values.

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation (Cross-site Scripting)

extra.message: Hardcoded secret credential. SUPER_SECRET_TOKEN is assigned the literal value "5u93R53Cr3tT0k3n" directly in source code (the adjacent FIXME comment indicates it was intended to be read from an environment variable via os.getenv). Hardcoding secrets in source exposes them to anyone with repository access and makes rotation impossible without a code change. Load secrets from a secure secret manager or environment variable instead.

Denial of Service via unbounded network call. requests.get(config.PUBLIC_IP_SERVICE_URL) is issued with no timeout argument, so if the external IP service is slow, unresponsive, or hangs the connection, the request handler thread blocks indefinitely. An attacker who can influence the availability of that service (or who triggers many concurrent requests) can exhaust the server's worker pool and take the application offline. Pass an explicit timeout (e.g. requests.get(url, timeout=5)) and handle timeouts gracefully.
